chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Grammar school in Houston, athletics and a Catholic school in Dallas
summary: He finished grammar school in Houston's Fourth Ward, played ball and high-jumped, and had earlier been to a Catholic school in Dallas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Listen, Gus, put it off for just one second, will you?
Well, I stopped you. We were just talking about Houston. So you and your Mom went to Houston.
And at that point, did you say you were still in grammar school?
Yes, I was still in grammar school.
And what did you do, have a year or two of grammar school there in Houston?
And so wasn't there a school band?
The school band was in -- it was in high school.
So -- but were you playing ball or --
Oh, I played ball, I was in track meets and all like that.
I used to love the high jump.
You did? You were a good athlete.
Oh, yes, I was in everything that come about.
Did it -- was it hard on you, going from school to school or could you fall right in, or did you have a few months of a bad time?
No, I didn't have any bad time at all, not changing schools.
Oh, that was good, especially for an only child. It was good, wasn't it?
Yeah, I went to a Catholic school.
Yeah, that was before I even went to Houston, when we --
We went to Dallas and then to Houston.
Like that, and I was quite young then, see. So when we left Dallas and went to Houston, --
I see, I see, yeah. What part of Houston was that?
We don't know Houston very well, but we did own that cob last year, so we got a little oriented, but not too much.
But there was always a lot going on in
Oh, there was quite a bit going on.
